season: Winter/early spring (an intentionally early-season route)
best_season: A winter route, with the best conditions typically arriving after a period of warm weather brings rain to the summit followed by a hard freeze, which bonds the snow and ice into more solid névé.

season: Aug (first ascent conditions); narrow window given the glacier/icefall approach and snow/ice finish
best_season: Climbed historically in early-to-mid August; conditions on the approach glacier/icefall and any residual snow/ice in the summit gully are season- and year-dependent, so this route likely climbs best in a similar window with a stable, well-bridged icefall.

season: Summer-Fall (rock)
best_season: Needs dry, snow-free ridge/scrambling conditions — effectively the same summer-fall window listed for Chair Peak's other rock routes.

season: Summer-Fall
best_season: Summer and fall, once the ridge is free of snow. Rock quality is poor enough that many parties wait for settled, dry weather.

season: Summer-Fall
best_season: Summer through fall once the approach snow patch has melted out and the rock is dry.

season: Spring-mid-summer
best_season: Spring into mid-summer; light crampons and a light axe are recommended until mid-summer per Pro Guiding Service, after which the route goes to dry rock.

season: Winter (Jan-Feb) established route; requires a stable high-pressure spell
best_season: A winter/early-spring ice-and-mixed route, climbed roughly December through March when the Hidden Couloir's ice pitches are well formed; the first ascent was done in late January.

season: Late June per the first-ascent account; broader climbing season is Jun-Sep
Jun-Sep climbing season generally; one trip report recommends May-early June specifically for water availability on the approach
Dec-Apr on ski/snowshoe; Jul-Oct on foot
best_season: This route has two seasons and both are good. Winter, roughly December through April, is the peak's main season and what this line is best known for — snow cover buries the brush and turns the whole thing into a straightforward skin and ski, and the north side holds the better snow quality through most of the winter. Summer and early autumn, July through October, give a short and pleasant rock and heather scramble; September is ideal, with the 1975 first documented ascent of the line falling on 20-21 September. Avoid late spring, when the snowpack is wet and heavy, avalanche hazard lingers on both flanks, and the ground below is still buried but no longer supportive.

season: Winter-early spring (roughly Nov-May), before the Cowlitz/Ingraham glaciers become too broken up to cross safely
best_season: Best attempted winter through early spring, when the Cowlitz and Ingraham glaciers are more consolidated; by late spring/summer the glaciers become significantly more broken and hazardous to cross, which is why most parties use the Frying Pan/Whitman (East Shoulder) route instead once the White River Road opens.

season: Jun-Sep for standard rock conditions; the route has also been climbed as a winter mixed snow/rock outing
best_season: Summer (roughly June-September) for standard dry-rock conditions; winter ascents have been done as a mixed snow/rock outing by experienced parties.

season: Summer/dry season only (technical rock route)
Jun-Oct for a dry scramble; also a common winter/spring snowshoe-and-axe ascent
best_season: Climbable year-round given favorable road access. Most parties go June-October once winter snow has cleared from the upper talus and ridge ponds and the private-timberland gate is more reliably open. Winter ascents are a popular snowshoe objective, but require checking current FR-62 gate status, expect lingering snow/ice, and may add significant road mileage if the highway gate is locked.

season: Late May–June is most commonly reported, when snow still covers the couloir and brush; by mid-summer the couloir is loose talus/scree
best_season: Late May into June offers a more direct snow-covered line over brush and talus, per multiple trip reports, but the couloir can be firm and icy that early, demanding solid crampon technique; by mid-to-late summer the couloir is loose talus and scree with no snow benefit.

season: Jul (best); serviceable Jun-Aug
best_season: Best in July-August once the Colchuck Glacier approach has consolidated and dried; rock is loose in spots and best climbed dry.

season: winter-spring
best_season: Winter through spring (roughly December-May) while SR 20 is closed to vehicles beyond the gate — this is the standard cold-season line up Ruby. Compact spring snow (April-May) is often cited as easier and lower-avalanche-risk than deep winter snowpack.

season: May-Jun while the couloir holds continuous snow/neve; becomes a loose rock gully once melted out
best_season: A snow/ice couloir route best done in late spring to early summer (roughly May-June) while it still holds continuous snow/neve.

season: Dec-Apr for the snow/mixed version; Jun-Oct as a rock scramble
best_season: Best as a snow and mixed climb from roughly December through April, once the gully has filled in and consolidated - which is exactly when avalanche hazard has to be managed carefully, since this is a south-facing gully directly below cliffs and adjacent to active ski-area terrain. The NWAC forecast for Snoqualmie Pass is a mandatory pre-trip read; do not climb this on a rising danger day or after significant new loading. Firm winter snow makes the approach and the climbing far faster than soft spring corn. From June through October the same feature is climbed dry as an easy-fifth-class scramble, which is a completely different and much lower-consequence outing.

season: Summer-Fall
best_season: Summer and fall; needs dry rock given the vegetated, low-quality climbing.

season: Best climbed in June with consolidated snow; conditions vary considerably year to year
best_season: June, with consolidated snow, is generally recommended; the route's character shifts significantly with how much snow remains on the ridge and in the Great Basin.

season: Best climbed roughly July through September/October once snow clears from Sawtooth Pass and the approach.
best_season: Parties note that snow lingering in Sawtooth Pass early season can actually ease the approach, while the route and approach slope turn loose/chossy later in the season; NPS rates the Olympic high country as best accessed early July through October.
